findings.reason: The protected Python solution uses dynamic programming with a rolling array of sets tracking reachable counts of ones for each grid cell. It first checks if the total path length (r + c - 1) is even, setting target = (r + c - 1) // 2. For each cell (r, c), it merges sets of reachable ones from (r-1, c) and (r, c-1) and adds grid[r][c], filtering out counts > target. The DP solution runs in O(r * c * (r + c)) time and O(c * (r + c)) space; no candidate is required.

Every valid path from (0,0) to (r-1, c-1) has length r + c - 1. An odd path length cannot be divided into equal numbers of 0s and 1s, returning False immediately. DP set propagation correctly calculates all reachable ones counts up to target.

At each of the r * c cells, sets of size at most O(r + c) are merged, yielding O(r * c * (r + c)) worst-case time complexity. Rolling array space uses O(c * (r + c)) space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts r x c binary matrix grid, returns boolean True if a balanced path exists and False otherwise.

The approach accurately details odd path length rejection, reachable ones count set propagation, rolling column array optimization, and O(r c (r+c)) time / O(c (r+c)) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover unmemoized DFS exponential explosion, 3D boolean tables, ones-minus-zeros tracking, odd path lengths, endpoint inclusion, and count deduplication.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the identical rolling-set DP reachability algorithm with SHA-256 digests bd8a72f36ac0320e60b1135759774c8b20592207a453dffd2adcf31d6dc554ef and c4a705212f2e57c621ef42980aacb913fe42a68bbbf4e11a63db498afa515eb2. Verified submission remains untouched.
